headline: No documented interaction pathway; both profiles are non-runnable, network-egress-none open-source artifacts with no shared surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile exposes an input channel, shared filesystem, or tool parser that could carry injected instructions. agent_a is a non-runnable knowledge-management artifact with no io_surfaces; agent_b is also non-runnable with no io_surfaces. With no bridge between them, prompt injection is provably blocked.
conditions: IF either profile gains a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge, reassess injection risk.
IF either agent becomes runnable with instruction-parsing I/O, the pathway may open.
mitigations: Keep both agents non-runnable in this pairing.
Do not add shared clipboard or filesystem mounts.
Review any future MCP or queue integration before enabling it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: No data-leakage pathway is evident because both profiles touch no data classes, request no permissions, and have network_egress set to none. agent_a and agent_b also expose no io_surfaces or shared workspace in the profiles, so there is no documented route for sensitive data to flow between them.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF either agent gains outbound network access, data exfiltration risk changes materially.
mitigations: Confirm no secrets are placed in any future shared directory.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Capability conflict is not plausible from the profiles: both agents have empty concurrency_model, no permissions_requested, and no write-capable surfaces listed. agent_a is a knowledge-management artifact and agent_b is a course repository; neither shows overlapping mutable resources or locks to contend over.
conditions: IF either agent is given write access to the same directory or git state, conflict risk must be reassessed.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locking-free mutable resources, contention may appear.
mitigations: Do not grant shared write access to the same path.
Add locking before any future shared mutable integration.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented pathway where agent_a's output becomes authoritative input for agent_b, or vice versa. Both profiles are non-runnable and expose no io_surfaces, so the cascade pattern described in the rubric is absent. Uncertainty is low because the profiles explicitly omit the needed handoff surfaces.
conditions: IF a future orchestrator feeds one agent's output directly into the other without verification, cascade risk increases.
IF either agent is made runnable and used for downstream actions, reassess.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between outputs and downstream use.
Keep both agents non-runnable in production.
Document any future handoff contract before enabling it.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced: both profiles are open-source, docs-only artifacts with no data_classes_touched, no permissions_requested, and no network egress. Because neither agent is shown handling regulated data or differing residency/retention regimes, the compliance pathway is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent's workflow, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF future deployment adds retention or residency differences, the risk profile changes.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pairing.
Record any future residency or retention policy before deployment.
Review compliance requirements before enabling new data flows.
